chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
title: Part 3 opens (7 May 1983); Al Dunn's quartet, Billie Holiday and Dinah Washington
summary: Back in Washington he plays a supper club with Al Dunn's quartet, accompanies Billie Holiday there, then joins Dinah Washington and is typed as an accompanist.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: John Malachi (5/7/83), Part 3, with Bryant DuPre:

After leaving Illinois, I came back to Washington, and then I took a gig in a club -- I was sort of a supper club type place -- with a bandleader. His name was Al Dunn. He had a title that everybody used to call him -- "Al, it's got to be done." Anyway, he had this quartet that had Frank Wess on tenor saxophone, and William Eldridge, a bassist, Roy Eldridge's cousin, on bass, and of course Al Dunn on drums. During that time this club featured major artists. It would bring in singers and sometimes even big bands.

While I was there, Billie Holiday came in. I think she was in there for two weeks, and we worked with her. After Billie Holiday left, I was with... I stayed there about two months, I guess, and I got a call from Dinah Washington. I went on a job with her, I guess, for about at least four or five weeks. I don't remember where we played. It seems like to me that we played some theatres or something.
Anyway, I was at that particular time beginning to be typed into some kind of a role as accompanist...
I was typed into this role as an accompanist to singers somehow. It must have been something that I was doing that they liked, perhaps not getting in their way or something like

that. Anyway, I worked a while with Dinah Washington, and oh... For a while, going into 1949, I kind of alternated between playing with Dinah Washington and Billie. It seems like a couple of times I would work with one for a few weeks and the other for a few weeks -- never over a long period. This kind of situation went on, and in between these times, either I would have a trio or I would be working with somebody's trio in and around Washington. And I did that up until 1950.
